title: The AI-Native Data Engineer featuring Fabric, dbt, VSCode devcontainers and copilot
summary: A Microsoft data engineer shows how dbt, testable Spark interfaces, local dev containers and parallel Copilot agents keep AI-written data pipelines reliable.

assertions.quote: align on things that are industry standards, like DBT, that everybody in the world recognizes

verdicts.note: Models do measurably better on libraries well represented in training data, and bespoke frameworks must be explained in context, though good docs narrow the gap.

assertions.quote: by the time it's done learning what you built, you've already filled up your context window

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: I don't want the LM to like take the entire wheel and reinvent it.

verdicts.note: GitClear's 2024-25 analyses found rising duplicated code and falling refactoring with AI adoption.

assertions.quote: First, you as the data engineer have to become competent of what you're trying to do.

verdicts.note: Studies show novices accept incorrect AI code more often; verifying output requires domain and code literacy.

assertions.quote: Ralph, until the steak is cooked exactly to the precise temperature with this thermometer that I've asked you for, do not stop.

verdicts.note: Goal/loop features keep agents going through backlogs, but unattended runs drift or game checks without good verification; works when acceptance tests are strong.

assertions.quote: I can go ahead and have 10 different Git work trees and Visual Studio Code

verdicts.note: Shared files and databases cause collisions; worktrees or containers per agent are the standard approach, and Codex and Claude apps build this in.

assertions.quote: if you do not have test coverage and you're throwing LLMs at writing more code, at some point it's going to become sloppy

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: I don't want the LLM to go and generate like 10,000 lines of Scala, right?

verdicts.note: GitClear and DORA 2025 data show more churn and duplication and lower delivery stability as AI adoption rises; more code means more to maintain.

assertions.quote: you want to have it in a function which is called transform, which takes in a data frame and spits out a data frame

verdicts.note: Clear module boundaries help both humans and agents navigate and test; consistent with Ousterhout and practitioner reports.

assertions.quote: I'm going to be the one that writes the the commit. I'm going to be the one that pushes it.

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.
